plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs light up the cold-season woodlands and gardens of Japan with rose-like blooms of crimson, pink and white. Their waxy petals surround a boss of golden stamens that stands out against dark green leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March in the wild, so mid-to-late January falls within the season
plants.location: Japan, coastal woodlands and gardens of Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan it is called tsubaki and has long been prized for the oil pressed from its seeds.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.commonName: African Lily, Lily of the Nile
plants.description: In the southern summer, tall bare stems rise above arching strap-like leaves. Each carries a rounded burst of 20 to 40 trumpet-shaped flowers. Gardens, roadsides and coastal slopes turn blue and violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mostly November to February, so it is in full flower on January 21
plants.location: Native to South Africa, and widely grown in southern Australia's summer gardens
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. The name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, bell-shaped white flowers with green-marked inner petals push up through frosty ground. They are among the first signs that winter is loosening its grip, and they often appear in drifts under bare trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, so it is in bloom around January 21
plants.location: Gardens and woodlands across the United Kingdom and temperate Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops can bloom through snow because their leaf tips are hardened and pointed, which helps them push up through frozen soil.
